column3: NKJV capitalizes “Me,” and renders “humble” as “the poor,” “bind up” as “heal,” and פְּקַח־ קוֹחַ (“opening,” of eyes or prison) as “the opening of the prison.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a year of favor” is rendered “the acceptable year.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a turban” (pe’er) is rendered “beauty,” keeping the pe’er/epher wordplay, and “oaks” “trees.”
Close to the Hebrew; “renew” is rendered “repair.”
Close to the Hebrew; “farmers” is rendered “plowmen.”
Close to the Hebrew; “nations” is rendered “Gentiles,” and “abundance” “glory.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “you shall have… honor,” and “ignominy” is rendered “confusion.”
NKJV reads בְּעוֹלָה as “for burnt offering” (be-olah, MT vowels) and renders “recompense” “their work.”
Close to the Hebrew; “nations” is rendered “Gentiles.”
